name: memory_archive_episodes
content: Create archive summaries from the following old episodic memory entries.
## Source Episodes ({episode_count} episodes)
{source_json}
## Instructions
1. Read through all episodes and group related ones into coherent task blocks
2. For each group, create a concise archive summary (1-2 sentences)
3. Record the time range, key entities involved, and outcome
4. Generate search keywords that would help retrieve this summary in the future
5. Aim for high compression: summaries should be 10-20x smaller than the originals
## Grouping Rules
- Episodes within the same task/workflow should be grouped together
- If a task spans multiple sessions, group by session boundaries
- Standalone episodes get their own archive entry
- Maximum 20 episodes per archive group
## Keyword Selection
Include keywords covering:
- Tool names used (e.g., calendar, browser, email)
- Action types (e.g., created, deleted, searched, navigated)
- Domain topics (e.g., scheduling, coding, research)
- Outcome indicators (e.g., success, failure, timeout)
- Entity names (people, projects, files)
Return the JSON object as specified by your system prompt.
Respond with ONLY valid JSON. No markdown, no code blocks, no prose.

variables.name: source_json
variables.description: JSON-serialized array of old episodic memory entries to archive
examples: [{"id": "ep_042", "content": "Navigated to calendar app", "timestamp": "2026-02-15T09:00:00Z"}, {"id": "ep_043", "content": "Created team standup event", "timestamp": "2026-02-15T09:02:00Z"}]

variables.name: episode_count
variables.description: Number of episodes in the source data

metadata.description: User prompt instructing the LLM to create compressed, searchable archive summaries from old episodic memory entries. Supports grouping, keyword extraction, and high compression ratios.
